item.title: Stockholm Syndrome and the Lebon Prizes
item.author: Aalok Varma and Anagha Varma
item.description: It’s that time of the year again when, each morning, the Nobel committee, based in Stockholm, announces whom they have decided deserves recognition for their work in science, literature, and peace. As a child, I was fascinated by these prizes, and the people who received them – after all, their names made it into textbooks, and they were made out to be the best of mankind – intelligent, curious, generous, resilient, <insert favourite glorious adjective here>. Over the years, though, as I began to understand the history and inner workings of this prize, these illusions have slowly unravelled.
